response.rationale: Male infant with severe bladder outlet obstruction: dilated thick-walled bladder, bilateral hydroureteronephrosis, urinary retention, oligohydramnios, and perirenal urinoma are classic for posterior urethral valves; normal physical exam argues against prune belly.

rejected.why: Prune belly syndrome would typically include abdominal wall muscle deficiency and often cryptorchidism; physical examination was normal.
UPJ obstruction does not explain the markedly dilated fetal bladder, bladder wall thickening, or urinary retention.
